key_insight: The paper reframes ad-hoc teamwork as online estimation of hidden, task-invariant partner capabilities so an agent can adapt across multiple tasks without prior population training.
engineering_relevance: This enables more robust human-AI teaming systems that can infer partner behavior quickly, reduce infeasible plans, and update decisions as collaborators or conditions change.
method: CE-CM uses simulation-based approximate Bayesian inference to estimate a partner capability vector from observed interactions.
The inferred capabilities are plugged into a contextual multi-agent MDP for planning with decentralized execution.
CE-CM-Div improves robustness by scoring capability hypotheses against diverse rollout behaviors instead of a single optimal trajectory.
evidence_signal: In simulation, CE-CM rapidly recovered hidden capabilities and reduced infeasible action assignments, and an offline human study with 225 trajectories from 15 participants showed CE-CM-Div improved capability estimates over CE-CM.
watch_item: Capability estimates depend on the quality and diversity of rollout simulations, so poor behavior models or limited task coverage could bias adaptation.
paper_title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
